entries.name: cat
entries.title: Category
entries.description: The category in the user interface where this quick style displays in the user interface.

attributes.name: pri
attributes.title: Priority
attributes.description: The priority within the category for this style determines the order in which it displays in the user interface.

attributes.name: type
attributes.title: Category Type
attributes.description: Category type.

entries.name: catLst
entries.title: Category List
entries.description: This element is simply a list of categories.

entries.name: desc
entries.title: Style Label Description
entries.description: This element defines a description for a style label definition. The description is simply a string describing the characteristics of the style label definition.

attributes.name: lang
attributes.title: Natural Language
attributes.description: The natural language of the title or description of this quick style.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Description Value
attributes.description: The string used for the description.

entries.name: presLayoutVars
entries.title: Presentation Layout Variables
entries.description: This element specified the layout property set. This set of properties determine different aspects concerning the layout of a diagram. All of the elements associated with enabling or disabling aspects of the user interface are also defined here.

entries.name: scene3d
entries.title: 3-D Scene
entries.description: The 3-D scene which consists of a camera, a light rig, and an optional backdrop to catch shadows.

entries.name: sp3d
entries.title: 3-D Shape Properties
entries.description: A set of 3-D properties which a shape can contain.

attributes.name: contourW
attributes.title: Contour Width
attributes.description: Defines the width of the contour on the shape.

attributes.name: extrusionH
attributes.title: Extrusion Height
attributes.description: Defines the height of the extrusion applied to the shape.

attributes.name: prstMaterial
attributes.title: Preset Material Type
attributes.description: Defines the preset material which is combined with the lighting properties to give the final look and feel of a shape.

attributes.name: z
attributes.title: Shape Depth
attributes.description: Defines the z coordinate for the 3D shape.

entries.name: styleDef
entries.title: Style Definition
entries.description: This element is the root tag for a style definition.

attributes.name: minVer
attributes.title: Minimum Version
attributes.description: The minimum product version that can support this quick style.

attributes.name: uniqueId
attributes.title: Unique Style ID
attributes.description: Unique ID that identifies a style.

entries.name: styleDefHdr
entries.title: Style Definition Header
entries.description: This element specifies header information associated with a style definition. The header information is used by an application to preprocess required data in order to help with possible performance concerns associated with an initial full load of a color transform definition.

attributes.name: minVer
attributes.title: Minimum Version
attributes.description: The minimum product version that can support this quick style.

attributes.name: resId
attributes.title: Resource ID
attributes.description: This attribute is the id which associates this header to the actual style definition part.

attributes.name: uniqueId
attributes.title: Unique Style ID
attributes.description: This attribute defines a unique identifier for the associated style definition.

entries.name: styleDefHdrLst
entries.title: List of Style Definition Headers
entries.description: This element is simply a list of style definition headers and is used to consolidate multiple headers into one group.

entries.name: styleLbl
entries.title: Style Label
entries.description: This element defines the actual style which is applied to a node in a diagram The style is referenced from within layout node. The style label contains formatting (without defining color) such as the 3D properties and text properties associated with a shape.

attributes.name: name
attributes.title: Style Name
attributes.description: The name of the style.

entries.name: title
entries.title: Title
entries.description: This element defines the title given to a style definition header. The title is simply a name for the style definition.

attributes.name: lang
attributes.title: Natural Language
attributes.description: The natural language of the title or description of this quick style.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Description Value
attributes.description: The string used for the description.

entries.name: txPr
entries.title: Text Properties
entries.description: This element defines special text formatting that can be applied to text through a style label.

entries.name: animLvl
entries.title: Level Animation
entries.description: This variable is used to indicate the animate by level string which is displayed to a user in the user interface.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Level Animation Value
attributes.description: This attribute indicates the string to use for level animation in the user interface.

entries.name: animOne
entries.title: One by One Animation String
entries.description: This variable is used to indicate the string to use for one-by-one animation in the user interface. This is used primarily when defining hierarchical diagrams to specify different ways animations applies to different levels of the diagram.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: One By One Animation Value
attributes.description: Specifies the type of one-by-one animation to use for a diagram.

entries.name: bulletEnabled
entries.title: Show Insert Node
entries.description: This element is used to indicate whether to enable user interface components associated with inserting a node in the data model.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Show Insert Node Value
attributes.description: This attribute is used to indicatewhether a user interface for inserting a node should be enabled.

entries.name: chMax
entries.title: Maximum Children
entries.description: This element is used to indicate when to enable and disable the user interface components associated with adding a new shape to a diagram. This element defines a max number of nodes a diagram can support through the user interface directly.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Maximum Children Value
attributes.description: This attribute indicates the maximum number of children the node can have before the user interface should be disabled.

entries.name: chPref
entries.title: Preferred Number of Children
entries.description: This variable indicates the number of children that the current node prefers to have. [Note: For example, this could be used to guide how many shapes to add by default to a diagram at various levels in the hierarchy. end note]

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Preferred Number of CHildren Value
attributes.description: This attribute indicates the number of children that the current node prefers to have.

entries.name: dir
entries.title: Diagram Direction
entries.description: This element indicates whether the diagram should switch direction. This element provides the ability to define different behavior for diagrams considering LTR or RTL directions.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Diagram Direction Value
attributes.description: This variable indicates whether the diagram should switch direction.

entries.name: hierBranch
entries.title: Organization Chart Branch Style
entries.description: This element defines the layout style of a branch in an organizational chart.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Organization Chart Branch Style Value
attributes.description: The value of this attribute indicates the layout style of a branch in an organization chart.

entries.name: orgChart
entries.title: Show Organization Chart User Interface
entries.description: This element is used to indicate when to show user interface controls specifically associated with organizational charts such as being able to add an assistant to a selected node.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Show Organization Chart User Interface Value
attributes.description: This attribute value specifies when to show the ‘Insert Assistant’ user interface control and the ‘Change Layout’ user interface for this diagram.

entries.name: ST_AlgorithmType
entries.title: Algorithm Types
entries.description: Types of available algorithms.

values.name: composite
values.title: Composite
values.description: The composite algorithm specifies the size and position for all child layout nodes.

values.name: conn
values.title: Connector Algorithm
values.description: The connector algorithm lays out and routes connecting lines, arrows, and shapes between layout nodes.

values.name: cycle
values.title: Cycle Algorithm
values.description: The cycle algorithm lays out child layout nodes around a circle or portion of a circle using equal angle spacing.

values.name: hierChild
values.title: Hierarchy Child Algorithm
values.description: The hierarchy child algorithm works with the hierRoot algorithm to create hierarchical tree layouts.

values.name: hierRoot
values.title: Hierarchy Root Algorithm
values.description: The hierarchy root algorithm works with the hierChild algorithm to create hierarchical tree layouts.

values.name: lin
values.title: Linear Algorithm
values.description: The linear algorithm lays out child layout nodes along a linear path.

values.name: pyra
values.title: Pyramid Algorithm
values.description: The pyramid algorithm lays out child layout nodes along a vertical path and works with the trapezoid shape to create a pyramid.

values.name: snake
values.title: Snake Algorithm
values.description: The snake algorithm lays out child layout nodes along a linear path in two dimensions, allowing the linear flow to continue across multiple rows or columns.

values.name: sp
values.title: Space Algorithm
values.description: The space algorithm is used to specify a minimum space between other layout nodes or as an indication to do nothing with the layout node’s size and position.

values.name: tx
values.title: Text Algorithm
values.description: The text algorithm sizes text to fit inside a shape and controls its margins and alignment.

entries.name: ST_AnimLvlStr
entries.title: Animation Level String Definition
entries.description: This simple type specifies the possible values for the string that should be displayed by a consumer for level animation of this diagram.

values.name: ctr
values.title: From Center Animation
values.description: This value specifies that the consumer shall allow "From Center At Once" or "From Center One by One" animation styles for this diagram.

values.name: lvl
values.title: By Level Animation
values.description: This value specifies that the consumer shall display "By Level" animation types for this diagram.

values.name: none
values.title: Disable Level At Once
values.description: This value specifies that the consumer shall disable level at once animation.

entries.name: ST_AnimOneStr
entries.title: One by One Animation Value Definition
entries.description: This simple type defines the possible values for the string to use for one by one animation in the UI. Default value is one.

values.name: branch
values.title: By Branch One By One
values.description: This value specifies that the one by one animation string in the user interface should read "By Branch One By One".

values.name: none
values.title: Disable One-by-One
values.description: This value specifies that the consumer should disable one by one animation.

values.name: one
values.title: One By One
values.description: This value specifies that the one by one animation string in the user interface should read "One By One".

entries.name: ST_ArrowheadStyle
entries.title: Arrowhead Styles
entries.description: This simple type defines different arrowhead style types for connectors.

values.name: arr
values.title: Arrowhead Present
values.description: Specifies that an arrowhead is to be used on the connector.

values.name: auto
values.title: Auto
values.description: Specifies that the algorithm defines if an arrowhead is to be used on a connector.

values.name: noArr
values.title: No Arrowhead
values.description: Specifies no arrowhead is to be used on the connector.

entries.name: ST_AutoTextRotation
entries.title: Auto Text Rotation
entries.description: This simple type defines how text rotates within a shape when the shape is rotated by an algorithm during layout.

values.name: grav
values.title: Gravity
values.description: Specifies that when the angle of the text hits the threshold of 90 degrees and 180 degrees, the text rotates by 180 degrees.

values.name: none
values.title: None
values.description: Specifies that text always rotates with the shape.

values.name: upr
values.title: Upright
values.description: Specifies that when the text angle hits 45, 135, 225, or 315 degree thresholds, then it rotates by negative 90 degrees.

entries.name: ST_AxisType
entries.title: Axis Type
entries.description: This simple type defines different node sets in relation to the current context node.

values.name: ancst
values.title: Ancestor
values.description: Specifies a set of nodes between the current context node and the root node, including the root node.

values.name: ancstOrSelf
values.title: Ancestor or Self
values.description: Specifies a set of nodes between the current context node and the root node, including the root node and the context node.

values.name: ch
values.title: Child
values.description: Specifies a set of children of the current context node.

values.name: des
values.title: Descendant
values.description: Specifies a set of all nodes beneath the current context node.

values.name: desOrSelf
values.title: Descendant or Self
values.description: Specifies a set of all nodes beneath the current context node, including the context node.

values.name: follow
values.title: Follow
values.description: Specifies the set of nodes which are peers after the context node and all descendants of the peers.

values.name: followSib
values.title: Follow Sibling
values.description: Specifies the set of nodes which are peers after the context node.

values.name: none
values.title: None
values.description: Specifies no node.

values.name: par
values.title: Parent
values.description: Specifies the parent node.

values.name: preced
values.title: Preceding
values.description: Specifies the set of nodes which are peers before the context node and all the descendants of the peers.

values.name: precedSib
values.title: Preceding Sibling
values.description: Specifies the set of nodes which are peers before the context node.

values.name: root
values.title: Root
values.description: Specifies the top-most node of the diagram.

values.name: self
values.title: Self
values.description: Specifies the calling context node.

entries.name: ST_AxisTypes
entries.title: Axis Type List
entries.description: This simple type represents a list of axis types. This simple type allows a list of items of the ST_AxisType simple type (§21.4.7.6).

entries.name: ST_BendPoint
entries.title: Bend Point
entries.description: This simple type defines where a bend is to occur within a connection between two nodes.

values.name: beg
values.title: Beginning
values.description: The bend is to occur at the beginning of the connection.

values.name: def
values.title: Default
values.description: The default bend is used.

values.name: end
values.title: End
values.description: The bend is to occur at the end of the connection.

entries.name: ST_Booleans
entries.title: Boolean List.
entries.description: A list of booleans. This simple type allows a list of items of the W3C XML Schema boolean datatype.

entries.name: ST_BoolOperator
entries.title: Boolean Constraint
entries.description: This simple type specified Boolean operations which can be applied to compare constraints.

values.name: equ
values.title: Equal
values.description: Equal operator.

values.name: gte
values.title: Greater Than or Equal to
values.description: Specifies the greater than or equal to Boolean operator.

values.name: lte
values.title: Less Than or Equal to
values.description: Specifies the less than or equal to Boolean operator.

values.name: none
values.title: None
values.description: Specifies a none Boolean operator

entries.name: ST_Breakpoint
entries.title: Breakpoint
entries.description: This simple type defines at what point the wrapping of nodes occurs for the snake algorithm.

values.name: bal
values.title: Balanced
values.description: Specifies that the number of nodes in every row and every column should be equal.

values.name: endCnv
values.title: End of Canvas
values.description: Specifies that nodes are added to the next column or row after filling the current column or row's space.

values.name: fixed
values.title: Fixed
values.description: Specifies to use a user defined number of nodes in a column or row.

entries.name: ST_CenterShapeMapping
entries.title: Center Shape Mapping
entries.description: This simple type defines the behavior of the cycle algorithm.

values.name: fNode
values.title: First Node
values.description: Specifies a node which is always in the center of a cycle diagram.

values.name: none
values.title: None
values.description: Specifies the normal layout of a cycle diagram.

entries.name: ST_ChildAlignment
entries.title: Child Alignment
entries.description: This simple type defines how to align a node in its allocated space.

values.name: b
values.title: Bottom
values.description: Specifies to align the node to the bottom.

values.name: l
values.title: Left
values.description: Specifies to align the node to the left.

values.name: r
values.title: Right
values.description: Specifies to align the node to the right.

values.name: t
values.title: Top
values.description: Specifies to align the node to the top.

entries.name: ST_ChildDirection
entries.title: Child Direction
entries.description: This simple type defines the layout direction of child nodes related to a specific parent node.

values.name: horz
values.title: Horizontal
values.description: Specifies that the child nodes are to be laid out Enumeration Value Description horizontally.

values.name: vert
values.title: Vertical
values.description: Specifies that the child nodes are to be laid out vertically.

entries.name: ST_ChildOrderType
entries.title: Child Order
entries.description: This simple type specifies the child order for a given layout node.

values.name: b
values.title: Bottom
values.description: Child order along the bottom.

values.name: t
values.title: Top
values.description: Top child order.

entries.name: ST_ClrAppMethod
entries.title: Color Application Method Type
entries.description: This simple type defines the way a given set of colors is applied to a set of nodes or items across a diagram.

values.name: cycle
values.title: Cycle
values.description: The colors apply from A to B to A if A and B were the colors present.

values.name: repeat
values.title: Repeat
values.description: The colors apply from A through B to A through B if A through B were the colors present.

values.name: span
values.title: Span
values.description: The colors interpolate from A to B across the entire diagram if A and B were the colors present.

entries.name: ST_ConnectorDimension
entries.title: Connector Dimension
entries.description: This simple type defines the dimensionality of the connection between two nodes.

values.name: 1D
values.title: 1 Dimension
values.description: Specifies a one dimensional connection, or rather a line.

values.name: 2D
values.title: 2 Dimensions
values.description: Specifies a two dimensional connection which has both width and height.

values.name: cust
values.title: Custom
values.description: Specifies a custom connection type.

entries.name: ST_ConnectorPoint

values.name: auto

values.description: Specifies that the algorithm determines the best connection site to use.

values.name: bCtr
values.title: Bottom Center
values.description: Specifies that the bottom, center connection site is to be used.

values.name: bL
values.title: Bottom Left
values.description: Specifies that the bottom, left connection site is to be used.

values.name: bR
values.title: Bottom Right

values.name: ctr

values.description: Specifies that the center connection site is to be used.

values.name: midR

values.name: tCtr

values.name: tL

values.name: tR

entries.name: ST_ConnectorRouting

values.name: curve

values.name: stra

values.name: fromT

entries.name: ST_PrSetCustVal
entries.title: Property Set Customized Value
entries.description: This simple type defines customization percentage values for certain elements in DrawingML. This simple type is a union of the following types: The ST_Percentage simple type (§22.9.2.9).

entries.name: acc
entries.title: Accent
entries.description: This element specifies the accent function, consisting of a base and a combining diacritical mark. If accPr is omitted, the default accent is U+0302 (COMBINING CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT). [Example: Example accent functions are 𝑎̇, 𝑎́ , and 𝑎̃. <m:acc> <m:accPr> <m:chr m:val="̃"/> <m:ctrlPr/> </m:accPr> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>a</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> </m:acc> end example]

entries.name: accPr
entries.title: Accent Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the Accent function. If chr is omitted, the default accent character is U+0302 (COMBINING CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT). [Example: The diacritical mark ~ (tilde) is: <m:accPr> <m:chr m:val="̃"/> </m:accPr> end example]

entries.name: aln
entries.title: Alignment
entries.description: This element specifies the alignment property on the box object. It is utilized only when the box is designated as an operator emulator. When 1 or true, this operator emulator serves as an alignment point; that is, designated alignment points in other equations can be aligned with it.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: alnScr
entries.title: Align Scripts
entries.description: This element specifies the alignment of scripts in the subscript/superscript function. When 1 or true, subscripts and superscripts are aligned to each other. When 0 or false, they are kerned to the shape of the base.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: argPr
entries.title: Argument Properties
entries.description: This element specifies any properties of the math argument. [Example: The XML below represents the argSz attribute on the base element e of a box:

entries.name: argSz
entries.title: Argument Size
entries.description: This element specifies the size, or script level, of an argument. If the element is omitted, the default argument size is 0. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default value of the val attribute is always 0.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies a value between -2 and 2 for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: bar
entries.title: Bar
entries.description: This element specifies the bar function, consisting of a base argument and an overbar or underbar, as in 𝑎 and 𝑎.

entries.name: barPr
entries.title: Bar Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties of the bar function. If this element is omitted, the bar assumes its default location of top (the mathematical overbar). [Example: 𝑥 (x with an underbar) is represented by the following XML representation: <m:bar> <m:barPr> <m:pos m:val="bot"/>

entries.name: baseJc
entries.title: Matrix Base Justification
entries.description: This element specifies the justification of the matrix. Text outside of the matrix can be aligned with the bottom, top, or center of a matrix object. If this element is omitted, the matrix assumes center justification.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the vertical justification parent element respect to surrounding text.

attributes.name: baseJc:
attributes.description: This matrix has top

attributes.name: baseJc:
attributes.description: This matrix has bottom

attributes.name: baseJc:
attributes.description: The possible values for this attribute are defined by the ST_YAlign simple type (§22.9.2.20).

entries.name: begChr
entries.title: Delimiter Beginning Character
entries.description: This element specifies the beginning, or opening, delimiter character. Mathematical delimiters are enclosing characters such as parentheses, brackets, and braces. If this element is omitted, the default begChr is '('.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies the character used by the parent element.

entries.name: borderBox
entries.title: Border-Box Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Border Box object, consisting of a border drawn around an instance of mathematical text (such as a formula or equation), as in 𝑎2 + 𝑏2 = 𝑐2 . If borderBoxPr is omitted then the default behavior of borderBox is a rectangular border (as shown in the “abc” example below).

entries.name: borderBoxPr
entries.title: Border-Box Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the Border Box object, which dictate the types of lines that can be drawn as part of the border. [Example: 𝑎2 + 𝑏2 = 𝑐2 (Diagonal Strikethrough from Top Left) and 𝑎2 + 𝑏2 = 𝑐2 (no left or right edges). end example]

entries.name: box
entries.title: Box Object
entries.description: This element specifies the box object, which is used to group components of an equation or other instance of mathematical text. A boxed object can (for example) serve as an operator emulator with or without an alignment point, serve as a line break point, have associated argSz, or be grouped such as not to allow line breaks within. If boxPr is omitted, all properties will be “false” by default.

entries.name: boxPr
entries.title: Box Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties of the Box object, for example, whether the Box serves as operator emulator with or without an alignment point, serves as a line break point, or receives the correct spacing for the mathematical differential. [Example:

entries.name: brk
entries.title: Break
entries.description: This element specifies whether there is a line break at the start of a run, or at the start of the Box object, such that the line wraps at the start of the run or box object. These user-defined line breaks occur when the XML tag <m:brk/> is encountered and does not follow a mathematical "order of precedence". If this element is omitted, a manual break is not inserted.

attributes.name: alnAt
attributes.title: Index of Operator to Align To
attributes.description: Specifies the index of the operator on the previous line of mathematical text which shall be used as the alignment point for the current line of mathematical text .

entries.name: brkBin
entries.title: Break on Binary Operators
entries.description: This element specifies how binary operators are treated when they coincide with a line break. If this element is omitted, the line break occurs before the binary operator. That is, the binary operator is the first element on the wrapped line.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies where to break on binary operators.

entries.name: brkBinSub
entries.title: Break on Binary Subtraction
entries.description: This element specifies how the subtraction operator is treated when it coincides with a line break, when brkBin is set to repeat. If this element is omitted, the subtraction operator is repeated before and after the break. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is --.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies how the subtraction operator is treated when it coincides with a line break, when brkBin is set to repeat.

entries.name: cGp
entries.title: Matrix Column Gap
entries.description: This element represents the (custom) column gap spacing information; the default value is 0 (which corresponds to 1 em). This value is interpreted differently depending on the value of cGpRule (§22.1.2.19). cGp is not used unless the value of cGpRule is 3 or 4. When cGpRule is omitted, the default spacing between matrix columns is 1 em (a val attribute value of 0).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the amount of space between columns of the parent element (for cGp/cSp) or rows (for rSp).

entries.name: cGpRule
entries.title: Matrix Column Gap Rule
entries.description: This element specifies the type of gap (horizontal spacing) between columns of a matrix; the default is 0. Horizontal spacing units can be ems or points (stored as twips).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the type of spacing between rows and/or columns.

entries.name: chr
entries.title: Character
entries.description: This element specifies the character to be attached to the base of an accent object, a group character object, or an n-ary operator object. When the parent element is accPr, the chr value should be within the range of (U+0300–U+036F) or (U+20D0–U+20EF). When the parent element is groupChrPr, the chr value should be a horizontal stretch character, such as U+2190 (LEFTWARD ARROW).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies the character used by the parent element.

entries.name: count
entries.title: Matrix Column Count
entries.description: This element specifies the number of columns to which a property applies. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is 1.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the number of columns to which a column property applies.

entries.name: cSp
entries.title: Minimum Matrix Column Width
entries.description: This element specifies the minimum column width of a matrix. The actual column width of a matrix will be the greater of either the width of the column’s widest argument or cSp. This additional spacing can be added to enhance appearance.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the amount of space between columns of the parent element (for cGp/cSp) or rows (for rSp).

entries.name: ctrlPr
entries.title: Control Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties on control characters; that is, object characters that cannot be selected. Examples of control characters are n-ary operators (excluding their limits and bases), fraction bars (excluding the numerator and denominator), and grouping characters (excluding the base). ctrlPr allows formatting properties to be stored on these control characters. The control character inherits its formatting from the paragraph

entries.name: d
entries.title: Delimiter Object
entries.description: This element specifies the delimiter object, consisting of opening and closing delimiters (such as parentheses, braces, brackets, and vertical bars), and an element contained inside. The delimiter may have more than one element, with a designated separator character between each element. [Example: Delimiter with one base: (𝑥2) Delimiter with more than one base and separators, whose XML is shown below: (𝑥2|𝑦2) <m:d> <m:e> <m:sSup> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>x</m:t> </m:r> </m:e>

entries.name: defJc
entries.title: Default Justification
entries.description: This element specifies the default justification of display math, at the document level. Individual instances of mathematical text can overrule the default setting. If this element is omitted, the default justification is centerGroup.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the default justification of mathematical text in the document.

entries.name: deg
entries.title: Degree
entries.description: This element specifies the degree in the mathematical radical. This element is optional. When omitted, the square root function, as in √𝑥, is assumed. [Example: The 3 in √𝑥 is represented by the XML below: <m:rad> <m:deg> <m:r> <m:rPr> <m:scr m:val="roman"/> <m:sty m:val="p"/> </m:rPr> <m:t>3</m:t> </m:r> </m:deg>

entries.name: degHide
entries.title: Hide Degree
entries.description: This element specifies the per-object option to hide the degree of a radical. Every rad has a deg, but the deg can appear or not appear. When degHide is set to 1 or true, the degree is not shown, as in √𝑥 (XML shown below).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: den
entries.title: Denominator
entries.description: This element specifies the denominator of a fraction. [Example: For example, the 𝑏 in 𝑎 𝑏⁄ : <m:f> <m:fPr> <m:type m:val="skw"/> </m:fPr> <m:num> <m:r> <m:t>a</m:t> </m:r> </m:num> <m:den> <m:r> <m:t>b</m:t> </m:r> </m:den> </m:f> end example]

entries.name: diff
entries.title: Differential
entries.description: The element specifies the differential property on box. When 1 or true, the box acts as a differential (e.g., 𝑑𝑥 in an integrand), and receives the appropriate horizontal spacing for the mathematical differential. When this property is omitted, the box is not treated as a differential.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: dispDef
entries.title: Use Display Math Defaults
entries.description: This element specifies the document-level property to overwrite paragraph settings for mathematical text. When omitted, this element is set to 1 or true and special math settings are applied. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is 1 meaning that this option is applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: dPr
entries.title: Delimiter Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of d, including the enclosing and separating characters, and the properties that affect the shape of the delimiters. [Example: [𝑎 + 𝑏] is represented by the following XML: <m:d> <m:dPr> <m:begChr m:val="["/> <m:endChr m:val="]"/> </m:dPr> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>a+b</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> </m:d> end example]

entries.name: e
entries.title: Element (Argument)
entries.description: This tag, which is an abbreviation for “element”, serves several functions (18 total) including that of the base argument of a mathematical object or function, the elements in an array, and the elements in boxes. If all subelements are omitted, this element specifies the presence of an empty argument. [Example: The numerator of this function is an empty argument: 2 . end example] [Note: The tag was shortened to e to improve readability over “element”. “Element” was preferred over “Base” because “Element” sounded more neutral and appropriate to its multiple uses. end note]

entries.name: endChr
entries.title: Delimiter Ending Character
entries.description: This element specifies the ending, or closing, delimiter character. Mathematical delimiters are enclosing characters such as parentheses, brackets, and braces. If this element is omitted, the default endChr is ')'.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies the character used by the parent element.

entries.name: eqArr
entries.title: Array Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Array object (sometimes referred to as "Equation Array", despite its ability to hold mathematical text other than equations), an object consisting of one or more equations, expressions, or other mathematical text runs that can be vertically justified as a unit with respect to surrounding text on the line. Alignment of multiple points within each run of mathematical text can occur within the array through the use of align values and spacer values. An align value is an ampersand within the array which acts as an alignment point (as described in §22.1.2.3).

entries.name: eqArrPr
entries.title: Array Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the array object, including the vertical justification of the object and layout inside the object. [Example: 111𝑎 = 𝑐 111𝑎 + 111𝑏 = 111𝑐 𝑏 = 111𝑐 <m:eqArr> <m:eqArrPr> <m:baseJc m:val="bottom"/> </m:eqArrPr> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>111&a&&&&&&=&&c</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>111&a&&+&111&b&&=&111&c</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> <m:e>

entries.name: f
entries.title: Fraction Object
entries.description: This element specifies the fraction object, consisting of a numerator and denominator separated by a fraction bar. The fraction bar can be horizontal or diagonal, depending on the fraction properties. The fraction object is also used to represent the stack function, which places one element above another, with no fraction bar.

entries.name: fName
entries.title: Function Name
entries.description: This element specifies the name of the function in the Function-Apply object func. For example, function names are sin and cos.

entries.name: fPr
entries.title: Fraction Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the fraction object f. Properties of the Fraction object include the type or style of the fraction. The fraction bar can be horizontal or diagonal, depending on the fraction properties.

entries.name: func
entries.title: Function Apply Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Function-Apply object, which consists of a function name and an argument element (e) acted upon. It is often applied using a form of linear format. For example, in the linear format described in Unicode Technical Article #28, this object is applied by using the Function Application character (U+2061).

entries.name: funcPr
entries.title: Function Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties such as ctrlPr that can be stored on the function apply object func. [Example: 𝑡𝑎𝑛 𝑥 is represented by the following XML:

entries.name: groupChr
entries.title: Group-Character Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Group-Character object, consisting of a character drawn above or below text, often with the purpose of visually grouping items. [Example: The following example demonstrates the groupChr in use, both in its proper form and in XML: 𝑥+𝑥+⋯⏞ <m:groupChr> <m:groupChrPr> <m:chr m:val="⏞"/> <m:pos m:val="top"/> </m:groupChrPr> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>x+x+&#22EF;</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> </m:groupChr> end example]

entries.name: groupChrPr
entries.title: Group-Character Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the Group-Character object groupChr. These properties can be used to specify the character placed above or below the argument, and the position of the character. When omitted, character ⏟ (U+23DF, BOTTOM CURLY BRACKET) is used as the chr and its pos is set to bot.

entries.name: grow
entries.title: n-ary Grow
entries.description: This element specifies the growth property of n-ary operators. When 0 or false, n-ary operators such as integrals and summations do not grow to match the size of their operand height. When 1 or true, the n-ary operator grows vertically to match its operand height.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: hideBot
entries.title: Hide Bottom Edge
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of the bottom edge of borderBox. When this element is omitted, the bottom edge is shown. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: hideLeft
entries.title: Hide Left Edge
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of the left edge of borderBox. When this element is omitted, the edge is shown. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: hideRight
entries.title: Hide Right Edge
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of the right edge of borderBox. When this element is omitted, the edge is shown. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: hideTop
entries.title: Hide Top Edge
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of the top edge of borderBox. When this element is omitted, the edge is shown. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: interSp
entries.title: Inter-Equation Spacing
entries.description: This element specifies spacing between equations, expressions, or other instances of mathematical text within a display math paragraph, in twips.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: intLim
entries.title: Integral Limit Locations
entries.description: This element specifies the document setting for the default placement of integral limits, when converted from a linear form to a two-dimensional output (professional form). Limits can be either centered above and below the integral, or positioned just to the right of the operator, as in: ∫ 𝑥 𝑑𝑥 𝑏 𝑎 ∫ 𝑥 𝑑𝑥 𝑏 𝑎

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the default location of limits on the parent object.

entries.name: intraSp
entries.title: Intra-Equation Spacing
entries.description: This element specifies the spacing between adjacent display math paragraphs, in twips. If this element is omitted, no spacing is applied between adjacent math paragraphs.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: jc
entries.title: Justification
entries.description: This element specifies justification of the math paragraph (a series of adjacent instances of mathematical text within the same paragraph). A math paragraph can be Left Justified, Right Justified, Centered, or Centered as Group. If this element is omitted, the math paragraph is Centered as Group.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the default justification of mathematical text in the document.

entries.name: lim
entries.title: Limit
entries.description: This element specifies the lower limit of the limLow object and the upper limit of the limUpp function.

entries.name: limLoc
entries.title: n-ary Limit Location
entries.description: This element specifies the location of limits in n-ary operators. Limits can be either centered above and below the n-ary operator (shown in the first summation below), or positioned just to the right of the operator (shown in the second summation below). ∑ 𝑥𝑛 𝑛 𝑖 = 0 ∑ 𝑥𝑛 𝑛 𝑖 = 0

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the default location of limits on the parent object.

entries.name: limLow
entries.title: Lower-Limit Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Lower-Limit object, consisting of text on the baseline and reduced-size text immediately below it. Examples of limLow include lim 𝑛→∞ and max 0≤𝑥≤1 . [Example: The XML that represents lim 𝑛→∞ is: <m:limLow> <m:e> <m:r> <m:rPr> <m:scr m:val="roman"/> <m:sty m:val="p"/> </m:rPr> <m:t>lim</m:t> </m:r> </m:e>

entries.name: limLowPr
entries.title: Lower-Limit Properties
entries.description: This element specifies control properties (ctrlPr) that can be stored on the Lower Limit (limLow).

entries.name: limUpp
entries.title: Upper-Limit Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Upper-Limit object, consisting of text on the baseline and reduced-size text immediately above it. [Example: Examples of limUpp include 𝑥+𝑥+𝑥⏞ 𝑘 times and = def . The XML that specifies the limUpp = def is:

entries.name: limUppPr
entries.title: Upper-Limit Properties
entries.description: This element specifies control properties (ctrlPr) that can be stored on the Upper Limit (limUpp).

entries.name: lit
entries.title: Literal
entries.description: This element specifies that the characters in the run are literal; that is, they are to be interpreted literally and not be built up based on any implied mathematical meaning. This is especially useful for operators or other special characters that signal a need for build up to an OMML reader. These characters are often encountered during a given instance of mathematical text when presented in a 1-dimensional linear format, such as the linear format defined by Unicode Technical Note #28 (Sargent 2006).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: lMargin
entries.title: Left Margin
entries.description: This element specifies the left margin for math, in twips. If this element is omitted, no left margin is used. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the option is 0.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: m
entries.title: Matrix Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Matrix object, consisting of one or more elements laid out in one or more rows and one or more columns. It is important to note that matrices do not have built in delimiters. Like other math elements, matrices are contained in a delimiter object (§22.1.2.24) when delimiters are desired.

entries.name: mathFont
entries.title: Math Font
entries.description: This element specifies the default math font to be used in the document. If this element is omitted, font substitution (§17.8.2) should be used to determine the most appropriate font for use throughout the document.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies the default math font to be used in the document.

entries.name: mathPr
entries.title: Math Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the document-level properties for all math in the document.

entries.name: maxDist
entries.title: Maximum Distribution
entries.description: This element specifies Array Maximum Distribution. When 1 or true, the array is spaced to the maximum width of the containing element (page, column, cell, etc.). The example image below illustrates an array expanded to fit the page, which is the containing element in this example.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: mc
entries.title: Matrix Column
entries.description: This element specifies a single column in a matrix m. [Example: An example of this element in use is: (1 2 3 4) <m:m> <m:mPr> <m:mcs> <m:mc> <m:mcPr> <m:count m:val="2"/> <m:mcJc m:val="center"/>

entries.name: mcJc
entries.title: Matrix Column Justification
entries.description: This element specifies the justification of a matrix column (or group of matrix columns) mc. When this element is omitted, the column is centered. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is center.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the horizontal alignment of the parent element.

entries.name: mcPr
entries.title: Matrix Column Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the matrix column mn, including the number of columns and the type of justification. [Example: As an extreme example, the following matrix has two columns that are left justified (count is 2) and three columns that are right justified (count is 3). ( 1 1 1 1 1 23 23 23 23 23 456 456 456 456 456 ) end example]

entries.name: mcs
entries.title: Matrix Columns
entries.description: This element specifies the collection of columns of the matrix m. [Example: An example of this element in use is: (1 2 3 4) <m:m> <m:mPr> <m:mcs> <m:mc> <m:mcPr> <m:count m:val="2"/> <m:mcJc m:val="center"/>

entries.name: mPr
entries.title: Matrix Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties of the matrix m, including the justification of the matrix and the layout of elements within the matrix. [Example: 𝑎 + 1 2 3 4 + 𝑏 is represented by the following XML: <m:oMath> <m:r> <m:t>a+</m:t> </m:r> <m:m> <m:mPr> <m:baseJc m:val="top"/> </m:mPr> <m:mr> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>1</m:t>

entries.name: mr
entries.title: Matrix Row
entries.description: This element specifies a single row of the matrix m. [Example: An example of this element in use is the following example, a 2x2 matrix. There are two rows; the first contains the elements 1 and 2; the second contains 3 and 4. (1 2 3 4) <m:m> <m:mPr> <m:mcs> <m:mc> <m:mcPr>

entries.name: nary
entries.title: n-ary Operator Object
entries.description: This element specifies an n-ary object, consisting of an n-ary object, a base (or operand), and optional upper and lower limits. Examples of n-ary objects are: ∫ 𝑥 𝑑𝑥 0 , ∑ (𝑛 𝑘)𝑘 , ∏ 𝐴𝑘 𝑛 𝑘=1 , and ⋃ (𝑋𝑛 ∩ 𝑌𝑛)𝑚 =1 . [Example: The example below demonstrates an n-ary object in its proper form and XML representation: ∫ 𝑥 𝑑𝑥

entries.name: naryLim
entries.title: n-ary Limit Location
entries.description: This element specifies the document setting for the default placement of n-ary limits other than integrals (since integrals are most often written as subSup and other n-ary operators are most often written as undOvr), when converted from a built down form to a two-dimensional output (professional form). Limits can be either centered above and below the n-ary operator, or positioned just to the right of the operator, as in: ∑ 𝑥𝑖 𝑛 𝑖=0 ∑ 𝑥𝑖 𝑛 𝑖=0

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the default location of limits on the parent object.

entries.name: naryPr
entries.title: n-ary Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the n-ary object. These include the n-ary operator character that is used (using the chr element), the shape and height of the operator (using the grow element), the location of limits (using the limLoc element), and whether empty limits display a placeholder character or are hidden (using the subHide and supHide elements). [Example: N-ary operators include: ∑, ∫ , ⋃, ⋀. end example]

entries.name: noBreak
entries.title: No Break
entries.description: This property specifies the "unbreakable" property on the Box object box. When 1 or true, no line breaks can occur within the box. This can be important for operator emulators that consist of more than one binary operator.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: nor
entries.title: Normal Text
entries.description: This element specifies that the run is normal text, i.e., math italics and math spacing are not applied. In a normal text run, no characters will trigger reformatting of a linear expression into a two-dimensional expression. When the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: num
entries.title: Numerator
entries.description: This element specifies the numerator of the Fraction object f. [Example: The 𝑎 in 𝑎 𝑏⁄ : <m:f> <m:fPr> <m:type m:val="skw"/> </m:fPr> <m:num> <m:r> <m:t>a</m:t> </m:r> </m:num> <m:den> <m:r> <m:t>b</m:t> </m:r> </m:den> </m:f>

entries.name: objDist
entries.title: Object Distribution
entries.description: This element specifies Array Object Distribution. When 1 or true, the contents of the array are spaced to the maximum width of the array object. When this element is omitted, the array does not receive object distribution.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: oMath
entries.title: Office Math
entries.description: This element specifies an instance of mathematical text. When used independently (not inside an oMathPara) with non-mathematical text preceding and/or following it, an independent oMath is interpreted as an inline math zone. All such math zones, including equations, expressions, arrays of equations or expressions, and formulas are represented by oMath blocks.

entries.name: oMathPara
entries.title: Office Math Paragraph
entries.description: This element specifies a math paragraph, or display math zone, that contains one or more oMath elements that are in display mode. The oMath containers of a display math zone are not themselves considered inline math zones..

entries.name: oMathParaPr
entries.title: Office Math Paragraph Properties
entries.description: This property specifies properties of the math paragraph oMathPara, including justification jc.

entries.name: opEmu
entries.title: Operator Emulator
entries.description: This element specifies the Operator Emulator property on box. When 1 or true, the box and its contents behave as a single operator and inherit the properties of an operator. This means, for example, that the character can serve as a point for a line break and can be aligned to other operators. (For more details on the properties of an operator, see Unicode Technical Report #25, §3.2.2 and §3.2.3, and Unicode Technical Note #28.) Operator Emulators are often used when one or more glyphs combine to form an operator, such as ==.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: phant
entries.title: Phantom Object
entries.description: This element specifies the phantom object. This object has two primary uses: adding the spacing of the phantom base element e without displaying that base; and suppressing part of the glyphfor spacing considerations.

entries.name: phantPr
entries.title: Phantom Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties of the Phantom object, including whether the phantom is hidden or visible, and the amount of space that is taken into account when laying out text and objects around phantoms.

entries.name: plcHide
entries.title: Hide Placeholders (Matrix)
entries.description: This element specifies the Hide Placeholders property on a matrix m. When this property is on, placeholders do not appear in the matrix. If this element is omitted, placeholders do appear such that the locations where text can be inserted are made visible.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: pos
entries.title: Position
entries.description: This element specifies the position of the bar or group character in the parent object; the default is bot. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is bot.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the position of the parent element.

entries.name: postSp
entries.title: Post-Paragraph Spacing
entries.description: This element specifies the spacing after a math paragraph, in twips. If this element is omitted, no spacing is applied after the paragraph.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: preSp
entries.title: Pre-Paragraph Spacing
entries.description: This element specifies the spacing before a math paragraph, in twips. If this element is omitted, no spacing is applied before the paragraph.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: r
entries.title: Run
entries.description: This element specifies a run of mathematical text.

entries.name: rad
entries.title: Radical Object
entries.description: This element specifies the radical object, consisting of a radical, a base e, and an optional degree deg. [Example: Examples of rad are √𝑥 (XML shown below) and √𝑥. <m:rad> <m:deg> <m:r> <m:rPr> <m:scr m:val="roman"/> <m:sty m:val="p"/> </m:rPr> <m:t>3</m:t> </m:r> </m:deg>

entries.name: radPr
entries.title: Radical Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties of the Radical object rad, including the hidden or shown state of the degree deg. [Example: √𝑏 is represented by the following XML: <m:rad> <m:radPr> <m:degHide m:val="1"/> </m:radPr> <m:deg/> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>b</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> </m:rad> end example]

entries.name: rMargin
entries.title: Right Margin
entries.description: This element specifies the right margin for math, in twips. If this element is omitted, no right margin is used. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the option is 0.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: rPr
entries.title: Run Properties
entries.description: This element specifies the properties of the math run r.

entries.name: rSp
entries.title: Row Spacing (Array)
entries.description: This element specifies spacing between rows of an array eqArr; it is used only when rSpRule is set to 3 (exactly; in which case the unit of measure is points) or 4 (Multiple; in which case the unit of measure is half-lines). If this element is omitted, single line spacing is used in the array, and no additional spacing is used in the layout of rows. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is 0.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the amount of space between columns of the parent element (for cGp/cSp) or rows (for rSp).

entries.name: rSpRule
entries.title: Row Spacing Rule
entries.description: This element specifies the type of vertical spacing between columns in a matrix. The following table demonstrates possible values of rSpRule along with their definitions and examples. Value Line spacing between rows Example (non-normative) 0 Single line gap 1 2 3 4 1 1.5 line gap 1 2 3 4

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the type of spacing between rows and/or columns.

entries.name: scr
entries.title: Script
entries.description: This element describes the script applied to the characters in the run. The XML includes the Unicode value of the character (between U+0000 and U+007F), along with the script of the character. The application maps the value and script type to the appropriate Unicode range.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the script type of the parent element.

entries.name: sepChr
entries.title: Delimiter Separator Character
entries.description: This element specifies the character that separates base arguments e in the delimiter object d. If this element is omitted, the default sepChr is '|'. In other words, when the element is absent, the default is for the delimiter object separator character to be U+2502 (BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies the character used by the parent element.

entries.name: show
entries.title: Phantom Show
entries.description: This element specifies the show property of the phantom phant. When 0 or false, the phant base e is hidden. If this element is omitted, the base e is shown.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: shp
entries.title: Shape (Delimiters)
entries.description: This element specifies the shape of delimiters in the delimiter object d. Delimiters can be centered around the math axis of the mathematical text and still be made to fit the entire height of their contents (see right-hand example below), or their height and shape can be altered to exactly match their contents (see left-hand example below). These settings significantly impact the shape of the mathematical text.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the shape of the parent element.

entries.name: smallFrac
entries.title: Small Fraction
entries.description: This element specifies a reduced fraction size display math, such that the numerator and denominator are written in script size instead of at the size of regular text. When the element is absent, the default value of the option is 0 meaning that this option is not applied. When the element is present and the val attribute is absent, the default of the val attribute is 1 meaning that this option is applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: sPre
entries.title: Pre-Sub-Superscript Object
entries.description: This element specifies the Pre-Sub-Superscript object, which consists of a base e and a subscript and superscript placed to the left of the base, as in 𝐴1 2 . [Example: The XML that specifies this function is: <m:sPre> <m:sub> <m:r> <m:t>1</m:t> </m:r> </m:sub> <m:sup> <m:r> <m:t>2</m:t> </m:r> </m:sup> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>A</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> </m:sPre> end example]

entries.name: sPrePr
entries.title: Pre-Sub-Superscript Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties such as ctrlPr that can be stored on the Pre-Sub-Superscript object sPre.

entries.name: sSub
entries.title: Subscript Object
entries.description: This element specifies the subscript object sSub, which consists of a base e and a reduced-size scr placed below and to the right, as in 𝑥𝑛. [Example: The XML that specifies this object is: <m:sSub> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>x</m:t> </r> </m:e> <m:sub> <m:r> <m:t>n</m:t> </r> </m:sub> </m:sSub>

entries.name: sSubPr
entries.title: Subscript Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties such as ctrlPr that can be stored on the Subscript object sSub.

entries.name: sSubSup
entries.title: Sub-Superscript Object
entries.description: This element specifies the sub-superscript object, which consists of a base e, a reduced-size scr placed below and to the right, and a reduced-size scr placed above and to the right, as in 𝑥𝑚𝑛 .

entries.name: sSubSupPr
entries.title: Sub-Superscript Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties of the Sub-Superscript object, including the alignment of scripts.

entries.name: sSup
entries.title: Superscript Object
entries.description: This element specifies the superscript object sSup, which consists of a base e and a reduced-size scr placed above and to the right, as in 𝑥𝑛. [Example: The XML that specifies this object is: <m:sSup> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>x</m:t> </r> </m:e> <m:sup> <m:r> <m:t>n</m:t> </r> </m:sup> </m:sSup> end example]

entries.name: sSupPr
entries.title: Superscript Properties
entries.description: This element specifies properties such as ctrlPr that can be stored on the Superscript object sSup.

entries.name: strikeBLTR
entries.title: Border Box Strikethrough Bottom-Left to Top-Right
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of a strikethrough diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner of borderBox. When this element is omitted, the strikethrough is not drawn. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: strikeH
entries.title: Border Box Strikethrough Horizontal
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of a strikethrough horizontal line in borderBox. When this element is omitted, the strikethrough is not drawn. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: strikeTLBR
entries.title: Border Box Strikethrough Top-Left to Bottom-Right
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of a strikethrough diagonal line from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner of borderBox. When this element is omitted, the strikethrough is not drawn. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: strikeV
entries.title: Border Box Strikethrough Vertical
entries.description: This element specifies the hidden or shown state of a strikethrough vertical line in borderBox. When this element is omitted, the strikethrough is not drawn. In other words, when the element is absent, the default value of the property is 0 meaning that this property is not applied.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: sty
entries.title: style
entries.description: This element describes the script applied to the characters in the run. The XML includes the Unicode value of the character along with the style of the character. The application maps the value and style to the appropriate Unicode range.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the style of the parent element.

entries.name: sub
entries.title: Subscript (Pre-Sub-Superscript)
entries.description: This element specifies the subscript of the Pre-Sub-Superscript object sPre. [Example: For example, the sub in the object 𝐴1 2 is 1. An example of this element in use is: <m:sPre> <m:sub> <m:r> <m:t>1</m:t> </m:r> </m:sub> <m:sup> <m:r> <m:t>2</m:t> </m:r> </m:sup> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>A</m:t> </m:r> </m:e> </m:sPre> end example]

entries.name: subHide
entries.title: Hide Subscript (n-ary)
entries.description: This element specifies the n-ary Hide Subscript property. When 1 or true, the lower limit does not appear, as in ∫ 𝑥 𝑥+1 𝑑𝑥 ∞ . If this element is omitted, the lower limit appears.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: sup
entries.title: Superscript (Superscript object)
entries.description: This element specifies the superscript of the superscript object sSup. For example, the sup in the superscript object 𝑥𝑛 is 𝑛. [Example: An example of this element in use is: <m:sSup> <m:e> <m:r> <m:t>x</m:t> </m:r> </m:e>

entries.name: supHide
entries.title: Hide Superscript (n-ary)
entries.description: This element specifies the n-ary Hide Superscript property. When 1 or true, the upper limit does not appear, as in ∫ 𝑥 𝑥+1 𝑑𝑥0 . If this element is omitted, the lower limit appears.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: t
entries.title: Text
entries.description: This element specifies the text in a math run r.

attributes.name: xml:space
attributes.title: Content Contains Significant Whitespace
attributes.description: Specifies how white space should be handled for the contents of this element using the W3C space preservation rules.

entries.name: transp
entries.title: Transparent (Phantom)
entries.description: This element specifies that the phantom is transparent for spacing. This means that if the contents of the phantom are belonging to a special spacing class (such as binary operators, relational operators, differentials, etc.), the contents of that phantom are taken into consideration when laying out text. If transparency is turned off, then the contents of the phantom are ignored during layout.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: type
entries.title: Fraction type
entries.description: This element specifies the type of fraction f; the default is 'bar'. Whether the element is absent or present without the val attribute, the default of the val attribute is bar. Fractions types are: Stacked Fraction: 𝑎 𝑏 Skewed Fraction: 𝑎 𝑏⁄ Linear Fraction: 𝑎 𝑏⁄ Stack Object (No-Bar Fraction): 𝑛 𝑘

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the type of fraction.

entries.name: vertJc
entries.title: Vertical Justification
entries.description: This element, combined with pos of groupChrPr, specifies the vertical layout of the groupChr object. Where pos specifies the position of the grouping character, vertJc specifies the alignment of the object with respect to the baseline. For example, when the group character is above the object, vertJc of top signifies that the top of the object falls on the baseline; when vertJc is set to bot, the bottom of the object is on the baseline.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the position of the parent element.

entries.name: wrapIndent
entries.title: Wrap Indent
entries.description: This element specifies the indent of the wrapped line of an instance of mathematical text. The line or lines of a wrapped instance of mathematical text after the line break can either be indented by a specified amount from the left margin, or right aligned. The default indent is 1".

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: Value
attributes.description: Specifies the value, in twips, of the parent element.

entries.name: wrapRight
entries.title: Wrap Right
entries.description: This element specifies the right justification of the wrapped line of an instance of mathematical text. The line or lines of a wrapped instance of mathematical text after the line break can either be indented by a specified amount from the left margin, or right aligned. If this element is present, the continuation is right aligned.

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: zeroAsc
entries.title: Phantom Zero Ascent
entries.description: This element specifies that the phantom has zero ascent. The ascent of the contents of the phantom is not taken into account during layout. When this property is omitted, the phantom does have ascent (zero ascent is not applied).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: zeroDesc
entries.title: Phantom Zero Descent
entries.description: This element specifies that the phantom has zero descent. The descent of the contents of the phantom is not taken into account during layout. When this property is omitted, the phantom does have descent (zero descent is not applied).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: zeroWid
entries.title: Phantom Zero Width
entries.description: This element specifies that the phantom has zero width. The width of the contents of the phantom is not taken into account during layout. When this property is omitted, the phantom does have width (zero width is not applied).

attributes.name: val
attributes.title: value
attributes.description: Specifies a binary value for the property defined by the parent XML element.

entries.name: ST_BreakBin
entries.title: Break Binary Operators
entries.description: This defines how to represent binary operators with respect to a line-wrapping break. The line can wrap before the operator or after the operator; alternately, the operator can appear both at the end of the first line and the beginning of the second.

values.name: after
values.title: After
values.description: When line-wrapping breaks occur on binary operators, the binary operator appears after the break (at the start of the next line).

values.name: before
values.title: Before
values.description: When line-wrapping breaks occur on binary operators, the binary operator appears before the break (at the end of the first line).

values.name: repeat
values.title: Repeat
values.description: When line-wrapping breaks occur on binary operators, the binary operator appears on both sides of the break (at the end of the first line and the start of the next line).

entries.name: ST_BreakBinSub
entries.title: Break on Binary Subtraction
entries.description: This simple type specifies how to represent subtraction on both sides of a line-wrapping break, when the Break Binary Operators option is set to repeat. The first character represents the sign at the end of the line with the break; the second represents the sign at the start of the wrapped line. Options are --, -+, and +-.

values.title: Plus Minus
values.description: Repetition of subtraction sign after a line-wrapping break is plus on the first line and minus on the second line.

values.title: Minus Plus
values.description: Repetition of subtraction sign after a line-wrapping break is minus on the first line and plus on the second line.

values.title: Minus Minus
values.description: Repetition of subtraction sign after a line-wrapping break is minus on the first and second lines.

entries.name: ST_Char
entries.title: Character
entries.description: This Simple Type specifies the single character used by the parent element.

entries.name: ST_FType
entries.title: Fraction Type
entries.description: Fractions can be of type bar (horizontal fraction bar), skewed ("skw" - diagonal fraction bar with kerned and vertically adjusted numerator and denominator), linear ("lin" - diagonal fraction bar, takes up exactly one line of space), and the "stack" object ("noBar").

values.name: bar
values.title: Bar Fraction
values.description: Fraction with a horizontal fraction bar.

values.name: lin
values.title: Linear Fraction
values.description: Fraction with slanted fraction bar, that takes up no Enumeration Value Description additional vertical space. noBar (No-Bar Fraction (Stack)) Stack object, which looks like a fraction with no fraction bar.

values.name: skw
values.title: Skewed
values.description: Fraction with diagonal fraction bar.

entries.name: ST_Integer2
entries.title: Integer value (-2 to 2)
entries.description: This simple type contains a value from (-2,+2) which specifies the size of the argument. The effects of each value are described by the referencing element.

entries.name: ST_Integer255
entries.title: Integer value (1 to 255)
entries.description: This simple type specifies an integer value. The semantics of each value are discussed by the referencing element.

entries.name: ST_Jc
entries.title: Justification
entries.description: This Simple Type specifies the justification of Math Paragraphs. Justification of the Math Paragraph can be Left, Right, Centered, or Centered as Group.

values.name: text
values.title: the Math Paragraph
values.description: with respect to the page.

values.name: left
values.title: Left Justification
values.description: Left justification of Math Paragraph

values.name: right
values.title: Right
values.description: Right Justification of Math Paragraph

entries.name: ST_LimLoc
entries.title: Limit Location
entries.description: Limits can be in one of two positions: Under-Over (undOvr - above and below the base), and Subscript- Superscript (subSup - positioned to the side of the base, in the position of subscripts and superscripts).

values.name: subSup
values.title: Subscript-Superscript location
values.description: Limits placed to the side of the base, as opposed to directly over and under.

values.name: undOvr
values.title: Under-Over location
values.description: Limits placed to the directly above and below the base, as opposed to on the side.

entries.name: ST_Script
entries.title: Script
entries.description: Script can be of type Roman, Script, Fraktur, Double-Struck, Sans-Serif, or Monospace.

values.name: double-struck
values.title: double-struck
values.description: Double-Struck Script Type

values.name: fraktur
values.title: Fraktur
values.description: Fraktur Script Type

values.name: monospace
values.title: Monospace
values.description: Monospace Script Type Enumeration Value Description

values.name: roman
values.title: Roman
values.description: Roman Script Type

values.name: sans-serif
values.title: Sans-Serif
values.description: Sans-Serif Script Type

values.name: script
values.title: Script
values.description: Script Type

entries.name: ST_Shp
entries.title: Shape (Delimiters)
entries.description: Delimiters shape can be centered around the argument, or matched to the shape of the argument.

values.name: match
values.title: Match
values.description: Match shape of contents of delimiters.

entries.name: ST_SpacingRule
entries.title: Spacing Rule
entries.description: Integer value (0 to 4), representing the type of spacing between rows.

entries.name: ST_Style
entries.title: Style
entries.description: Style of math can be plain, bold, italic, or bold-italic (p, bi, i, or bi).
